clarity_hierarchy.critique: The composition suffers from severe visual fragmentation and a lack of a unified focal point. The primary action button ('START ADVENTURE') is visually buried by the 'Controls Guide' in the bottom right, which uses high-contrast white text on a dark background that competes aggressively for attention. The 'World Selector' (three circles) in the bottom left is visually ambiguous and disconnected from the hero character, creating a confusing relationship between the character and the selection mechanism. The top-left title and top-right stats create a wide horizontal spread that forces the eye to scan the entire width before settling on the center, while the massive empty blue space in the middle creates a 'dead zone' that disconnects the header from the gameplay elements.
clarity_hierarchy.suggestion: 1. Establish a clear vertical hierarchy: Move the 'Controls Guide' to a secondary position (e.g., smaller, lower opacity, or tucked behind the button) so the 'START ADVENTURE' button is the undisputed visual anchor. 2. Group the 'World Selector' directly adjacent to the hero character or the level preview to clarify that these circles represent the character's state or the current level. 3. Tighten the layout by moving the 'Score/Coins' box closer to the title or integrating it into the header to reduce the visual gap between the top and bottom thirds. 4. Increase the scale of the hero character and level preview to fill the central 'dead zone', ensuring the eye flows naturally from the Title -> Hero/Level -> Start Button.

visual_system_craft.critique: The visual system suffers from a lack of cohesive geometry and inconsistent component grammar. The 'Start Adventure' button uses a heavy, 3D extrusion style (reminiscent of skeuomorphism) that clashes with the flat, vector aesthetic of the UI panels and the game world. The typography is fragmented: the title uses a heavy serif, the subtitle uses a condensed sans-serif, and the UI elements use a standard sans-serif, creating a disjointed typographic hierarchy. The UI containers (top right score, bottom left abilities, bottom right controls) use inconsistent border radii and opacity levels, failing to establish a unified 'glass' or 'panel' language. The bottom ground layer is a flat, muddy brown that lacks the texture or detail of the rest of the scene, and the green 'grass' tufts appear to be rough, unrefined brush strokes rather than integrated assets. The alignment of the 'Start Adventure' button is ambiguous, floating without a clear anchor to the grid or the ground plane.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: 1. Unify the UI component language: Adopt a consistent 'glassmorphism' or 'solid card' style for all UI panels (score, controls, abilities) with matching border radii (e.g., 16px), consistent background opacity, and a unified drop shadow. 2. Harmonize the button style: Redesign the 'Start Adventure' button to match the UI panel aesthetic—use a flat or subtle gradient style with a crisp border rather than a heavy 3D extrusion, ensuring it feels like part of the same system as the other UI elements. 3. Standardize typography: Select a single, versatile typeface family (e.g., a rounded geometric sans) and use weight/size variations for hierarchy instead of mixing three distinct font styles. 4. Refine the ground layer: Replace the flat brown bar with a textured asset or a gradient that matches the game's color palette, and ensure the grass tufts are stylized vector shapes that align with the 'expressive shapes' requirement. 5. Establish a spacing grid: Align the UI elements to a consistent margin system (e.g., 40px from edges) and ensure the 'Start Adventure' button is centered or anchored with clear intent.

You are reviewing a work-in-progress web screen. Your ONE job is Visual System & Craft: defend coherence, consistency, precision, material quality, and shipping-level finish. Other reviewers defend brief alignment, hierarchy, and expressiveness. Stay strictly in your lane.

WHAT YOU CARE ABOUT — Visual System & Craft:
Defend consistent geometry and component grammar; disciplined palette and semantic color roles; typography pairing, scale, weight, contrast, and line height; spacing rhythm, alignment, grids, borders, shadows, strokes, radii, icons, and illustration cohesion; and the absence of clipping, collisions, jank, rough edges, or unfinished regions. A coherent but unoriginal design may still succeed on this axis. Defend restraint when unnecessary local variation fragments the system.

You are looking at a screenshot of the CURRENT DRAFT for this brief:
BRIEF:
Design a single-page introduction screen for a colorful side-scrolling platform adventure inspired by classic mascot platformers. Include a bold original game title, a hero beside a layered level preview with platforms, blocks, coins, enemies, and a distant goal, plus a prominent Start Adventure button, small controls guide, world selector, and collectible counters. Put strong emphasis on a joyful original identity, clear gameplay storytelling, depth, expressive shapes, and a polished launch-screen composition.

Critique ONLY Visual System & Craft from visible evidence. Identify concrete inconsistencies, alignment errors, color or typography problems, construction mistakes, and unfinished details. Prescribe impactful system-level and finishing changes. Do not judge missing requirements, conceptual reading order, or originality unless they directly cause a system or craft failure.

Return JSON only, with both fields non-empty and no other text:
{"critique":"<specific visible Visual System & Craft failures>","suggestion":"<concrete prioritized system-level and finishing changes>"}

expressiveness.critique: The design suffers from severe 'dashboard-ification' of a creative experience. The UI elements (HUD, Controls, World Selector) are trapped in generic, rounded-rectangle containers with identical drop shadows, creating a flat, administrative look that kills the sense of adventure. The 'Green Hills' world selector uses a dull, muddy brown that clashes with the vibrant sky, and the 'Controls' panel looks like a sterile settings menu rather than an in-game tutorial. The hero character is visually passive and lacks the dynamic energy required for a platformer. The composition is too tidy and safe, lacking the chaotic joy and depth of a classic mascot adventure.
expressiveness.suggestion: 1. **Dissolve the UI Boxes**: Remove the white containers and drop shadows. Integrate the HUD into the sky (e.g., a wooden signpost or floating clouds) and the Controls into the ground (e.g., a painted crate or a character holding a sign). 2. **Inject Dynamic Energy**: Pose the hero mid-jump or mid-action to imply movement. Add motion lines or a 'dust' effect under the feet. 3. **Thematic Typography**: Replace the standard sans-serif title with a chunky, custom display font that feels bouncy and rubbery. 4. **Vibrant World Selector**: Replace the dull brown box with a stylized map fragment or a glowing portal icon that matches the 'Green Hills' theme. 5. **Depth & Texture**: Add foreground elements (like tall grass or vines) overlapping the UI to create a sense of scale and immersion, moving away from the flat 2D plane.

Treat uniform cards, timid contrast, repetitive rhythm, superficial theming, and anonymous polish as failures. Reject random colors and decoration without semantic purpose.

INDEPENDENT AXIS REVIEWS (apply all; no moderator has summarized or resolved them):

[Brief & Intent Alignment | brief_intent]
CRITIQUE:
The design fails to deliver the requested 'layered level preview' and 'depth.' The background is a flat, empty blue void that lacks the atmospheric layering (distant mountains, clouds, parallax elements) required to establish the 'adventure' scale. The 'hero' is visually weak and ambiguous; the red character is small, lacks a distinct mascot silhouette, and is partially obscured by the UI, failing to command attention as the protagonist. The 'distant goal' is a tiny flag on the horizon, which does not effectively communicate the objective or the scope of the level. The 'world selector' is reduced to three abstract colored squares, which fails to convey the 'world' concept or offer a meaningful selection experience. The 'collectible counters' are placed in a HUD-style bar at the top, which feels like a gameplay overlay rather than a polished launch-screen element, clashing with the 'joyful original identity' intent.
SUGGESTION:
1. Construct a rich, multi-layered background with distant mountains, clouds, and foreground elements to create the requested 'depth' and 'layered level preview.' 2. Scale up the hero character significantly, placing them in a dynamic, expressive pose in the foreground to establish a strong mascot identity. 3. Replace the abstract colored squares in the world selector with distinct icons or thumbnails representing different environments. 4. Move the collectible counters (coins/lives) into a more integrated UI element or badge near the hero, rather than a floating HUD bar, to maintain the 'launch-screen' aesthetic. 5. Make the 'distant goal' more prominent or visually connected to the hero's gaze to better tell the gameplay story.

[Clarity & Information Hierarchy | clarity_hierarchy]
CRITIQUE:
The composition suffers from severe visual fragmentation and a lack of a clear reading path. The 'Start Adventure' button is the most critical element but is visually buried in the middle of the screen, competing with the Title, the HUD, and the World Selector. The 'Controls' panel in the bottom right is disproportionately large and bright, creating a 'dead area' of information that distracts from the gameplay preview. The 'World Selector' in the bottom left is visually disconnected from the 'Green Hills' label in the top left, creating a confusing relationship between the two. The HUD in the top right feels like an overlay rather than part of the scene, creating a cluttered 'frame' effect that pushes the eye away from the center.
SUGGESTION:
Establish a strict Z-pattern reading flow: Title (Top Left) -> Hero/Preview (Center) -> CTA (Center/Bottom). 1. Move the 'Start Adventure' button to the bottom center, anchoring the composition and making it the clear final destination of the eye. 2. Group the 'World Selector' buttons directly under the 'Green Hills' label in the top left to unify the navigation context. 3. Reduce the 'Controls' panel size by 50% and move it to the bottom right corner, ensuring it doesn't compete with the hero character. 4. Integrate the HUD (Coins/Lives) into the top right corner with lower opacity or a smaller scale so it doesn't fight the Title for attention. 5. Ensure the Hero character is positioned to the left of the CTA, visually leading the eye toward the button.

[Visual System & Craft | visual_system_craft]
CRITIQUE:
The visual system suffers from a lack of cohesive geometry and inconsistent component grammar. The 'Start Adventure' button uses a heavy, flat drop shadow and a specific corner radius that clashes with the sharp, hard-edged 'Controls' panel and the rounded, pill-shaped HUD in the top right. There is no unified grid; the 'Green Hills' tag floats without alignment to the title, and the 'Select World' label is misaligned with its container. The typography is fragmented: the title uses a heavy, outlined sans-serif, while the HUD and controls use a thin, unstyled system font that lacks the 'mascot platformer' personality. The 'Select World' container has a thick white stroke that feels like a placeholder, and the internal color swatches have inconsistent inner shadows. The HUD panel in the top right has a harsh black stroke that contradicts the soft, cartoon aesthetic of the clouds and background.
SUGGESTION:
Establish a unified 'Game UI' style guide: standardize all corner radii (e.g., 12px for panels, 50% for pills) and apply a consistent stroke weight (2px-4px dark outline) to all UI elements to match the game art style. Replace the generic system font in the HUD and Controls with a rounded, playful display font that matches the title's energy. Unify the button hierarchy: give the 'Start Adventure' button a 3D 'extrusion' effect (solid offset) rather than a soft shadow to match the platformer genre. Align the 'Select World' container to a strict grid relative to the bottom edge, and ensure the internal color swatches share the exact same inner shadow and highlight logic. Finally, refine the HUD panel by removing the harsh black stroke in favor of a thick, colored outline or a drop-shadow-only approach to integrate it better with the sky background.

Add motion lines or a 'dust' effect under the feet. 3. **Thematic Typography**: Replace the standard sans-serif title with a chunky, custom display font that feels bouncy and rubbery. 4. **Vibrant World Selector**: Replace the dull brown box with a stylized map fragment or a glowing portal icon that matches the 'Green Hills' theme. 5. **Depth & Texture**: Add foreground elements (like tall grass or vines) overlapping the UI to create a sense of scale and immersion, moving away from the flat 2D plane.
